title: Short Stuff: Chia Pet
summary: Short Stuff episode on the Chia Pet, the terra cotta planter figurines grown with chia seed sprouts. The hosts cover the origin of the product, with Joe Pettit (spelled Joe Pettot in the transcript) founding Joseph Enterprises in the 1970s after buying from a Chicago trade show, the early chia animals and the first chia man figure, licensing deals (Looney Tunes characters, sports teams, company logos, Star Wars Grogu), annual holiday-driven sales, the "Ch-ch-Chia" jingle, presidential-candidate and animal prediction gimmicks, and how to grow one (soak the terra cotta, spread a seed paste, water in sun, sprouts brown after about four to six weeks, reuse with new seed). Ends with the Smithsonian and a time capsule mention.
topics: how to grow a Chia Pet

segments.title: Opening banter and Chia Pet introduction
segments.summary: The hosts introduce the Short Stuff series and the Chia Pet topic, describing the figurine planters and sprouting chia hair, then chat about Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3.

segments.title: Origins and Joseph Enterprises
segments.summary: The terra cotta planters were made in Wojacque, Mexico. Joe Pettit founded Joseph Enterprises in the 1970s after seeing the planters at a Chicago trade show and deciding to brand and sell them as Chia Pets.

segments.title: Holiday sales and first Chia figures
segments.summary: Retailers pointed Pettit to a product that sold reliably each year. Chia Pets sell most around the holidays, with little advertising needed. The first figure was a goofy man, followed by Chia animals like the bull and ram, then licensed Looney Tunes characters Taz, Elmer Fudd and Tweety in the early 1980s.

segments.title: Licensing, predictions and company logos
segments.summary: Chia Pets are licensed to sports teams and companies can order a logo Chia Pet. The hosts mention Chia figures that predict presidential elections, the World Cup, the Super Bowl and the weather.

segments.title: How to grow a Chia Pet
segments.summary: Soak the terra cotta planter for a few hours because terra cotta draws water away from the plant. Soak the chia seeds, spread them as a paste with fingers or a spreader, put it in sun and water. Sprouts turn brown after about four to six weeks, and the pet can be reset with new seed. The hosts speculate about nutrients limiting growth beyond the sprout stage.
topics: how to grow a Chia Pet

segments.title: Jingle, Smithsonian and time capsule
segments.summary: The Ch-ch-Chia jingle is credited with driving sales. The Smithsonian National Museum of American History acquired Chia Pet items, including advertising tapes, and a Chia Pet is to be included in a New York City time capsule to be opened in the year 3000.

segments.title: Closing thoughts
segments.summary: The hosts praise the Chia Pet as a cultural staple and joke about following a Richard Simmons Chia Pet on Instagram.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts close the episode and the show credits iHeartRadio.
